Project registry of models, scenarios, and runs

Source: R/registry.R
registry.Rd

The registry is a per-project CSV file (see get_registry_file()) indexing the saved models, scenarios, and runs: one row each, with type, name, content hash (models), path, parent (runs), timestamps, and a memo. It is a rebuildable index — the on-disk manifests are the source of truth, and refresh_registry() reconstructs the registry by rescanning the scenarios/ and models/ stores.

  • newRegistry() constructs a new, empty registry. Creating one is explicit: load_registry() does NOT invent a registry for you.

  • load_registry() reads the registry file into a tibble, and errors when the file does not exist — naming newRegistry(). (Object stores create their own registry on first write, so save_model() and friends work in a fresh project without any ceremony.)

  • save_registry() writes the tibble back.

  • add_to_registry() inserts or updates one row (keyed by type + name + parent) and returns the updated tibble; it does not write the file.

  • find_in_registry() filters by any combination of type, name, hash, and parent (exact matches; NULL = no filter).

  • refresh_registry() rescans the stores under root and rebuilds rows from what is actually on disk, preserving created/memo of surviving entries; with write = TRUE (default) the result is saved.

Usage

newRegistry()

load_registry(file = get_registry_file())

save_registry(reg, file = get_registry_file())

add_to_registry(
  reg,
  type,
  name,
  path,
  hash = "",
  model = "",
  model_hash = "",
  parent = "",
  variant = "",
  memo = "",
  sealed = FALSE,
  sealed_at = "",
  marked_delete = FALSE,
  delete_importance = NA_real_,
  marked_at = "",
  status = ""
)

# S3 method for class 'en_registry'
add(obj, ...)

# S3 method for class 'en_registry'
summary(object, ...)

find_in_registry(
  reg,
  type = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  hash = NULL,
  parent = NULL,
  variant = NULL
)

refresh_registry(
  root = ".",
  file = get_registry_file(),
  write = TRUE,
  lazy = FALSE
)

Arguments

file

character, path to the registry CSV (default get_registry_file()).

reg

a registry tibble as returned by load_registry().

type

character: "model", "repository", "scenario", or "run".

name

character, object name (for runs: "<variant>/<solve>").

path

character, object directory, relative to the registry file's directory.

hash

character, model content hash (from model_hash(), arriving with the model store); "" for scenario/run rows.

model_hash

character, for scenario rows: hash of the referenced or embedded model.

parent

character, for run rows: the scenario name.

variant

character, for run rows: the variant the run belongs to.

memo

character, optional free-form note.

sealed, sealed_at, marked_delete, delete_importance, marked_at

Lifecycle state, mirrored from the entry's own manifest — which stays the source of truth. Cached in the registry so the CSV answers "sealed?" and "marked for deletion?" on its own. Set by seal_model() and mark_delete() rather than passed by hand.

status

character, for run rows: the solve status from run.yml.

obj

the object a registry row is derived from.

...

unused.

object

a loaded registry.

root

character, project root to rescan (the directory holding the scenarios/ and models/ stores).

write

logical, save the refreshed registry to file.

lazy

logical. FALSE (default) always rescans — a full scan is around 0.3 s for ~80 manifests, too cheap to risk serving a stale table. TRUE skips the scan when the registry is already up to date with the stores, for callers that refresh repeatedly. The check compares the CSV's own modification time, which changes without the content changing (a git checkout, a file copy, cloud sync, saving from Excel), so a registry copied in from elsewhere can read as fresh.

Value

load_registry(), add_to_registry(), find_in_registry(), and refresh_registry() return the registry tibble; save_registry() returns file invisibly.

Details

add() dispatches on a loaded registry, so add(reg, "scenario", "BASE", path = "scenarios/BASE") is add_to_registry() under the generic shared with models and repositories.

summary() reports the registry rather than listing it: counts by type, how many entries are sealed or queued for deletion, how the runs ended, and — because the lifecycle columns are a cache of each entry's manifest — a warning when the stores have moved on since the file was written.

Examples

reg <- newRegistry()
reg <- add_to_registry(reg, "scenario", "BASE", path = "scenarios/BASE")
find_in_registry(reg, type = "scenario")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 18
#>   type     name  hash  model model_hash path      parent variant created updated
#>   <chr>    <chr> <chr> <chr> <chr>      <chr>     <chr>  <chr>   <chr>   <chr>  
#> 1 scenario BASE  ""    ""    ""         scenario… ""     ""      2026-1… 2026-1…
#> # ℹ 8 more variables: energyRt_version <chr>, sealed <lgl>, sealed_at <chr>,
#> #   marked_delete <lgl>, delete_importance <dbl>, marked_at <chr>,
#> #   status <chr>, memo <chr>
